implemented_requirements.requirement: Player ship positioned at the bottom of the screen
implemented_requirements.evidence: sprites.Player creates its rect with midbottom=(settings.PLAYER_START_X, settings.PLAYER_START_Y) where PLAYER_START_Y = HEIGHT - 40 (bottom area).
Player.update() checks pygame.key.get_pressed() for LEFT/RIGHT or A/D and adjusts rect.x by settings.PLAYER_SPEED, then clamps inside screen bounds.
Game.handle_events() creates a Bullet via player.shoot() on SPACE; Player.shoot() respects cooldown and returns a Bullet instance.
Game.update() uses pygame.sprite.groupcollide(self.bullets, self.fleet.aliens, True, True) to remove both bullet and alien on collision.
settings.ALIEN_ROWS = 4 and ALIEN_COLS = 8; Fleet._build() creates a grid of Alien sprites for each row and column.
Game.reset() sets self.lives = settings.STARTING_LIVES (3). Lives are decremented on bomb hit and displayed in HUD.
Game.update() adds alien.points to self.score on each alien hit; draw_hud() renders the score on screen.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends if aliens reach the bottom
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.update() checks self.fleet.has_reached(settings.ALIEN_REACH_Y) and sets state to "game_over".

implemented_requirements.requirement: Victory when all aliens are destroyed
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.update() sets state to "victory" when not self.fleet.aliens.
Fleet._drop_bombs() creates Bomb sprites; Game.update() detects collisions with player.

critical_issues: The repository contains duplicate sprite definitions (alien.py, bomb.py, bullet.py) that lack required imports; they are not used by the game but could cause import errors if referenced.
No explicit unit tests or entry‑point guard for non‑pygame environments beyond the friendly message in main.py.
judge.summary: All core features of the simplified Space Invaders game are present: a bottom‑aligned player ship with horizontal movement and shooting, multiple rows of aliens, lives, scoring, game‑over on alien reach, and victory on clearing the fleet. The code is organized, uses pygame correctly, and should run when pygame is installed. Minor issues are limited to unused duplicate modules that do not affect execution.
